cards.explanation: The answer is to block anyone going in or out of Judah. Baasha fortified Ramah "…to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah." Imagine somebody parking a truck across the only road out of your neighborhood. Nobody's getting in, and nobody's getting out.

The answer is the treasuries of the temple and the palace. Asa withdrew the silver and gold "…from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace…" That means he reached into both places and took it out. I think that's a lot of silver and gold to hand over to somebody else.

The answer is Ben-hadad king of Aram. Asa sent the silver, the gold and his message to Ben-hadad, who was ruling in Damascus. Aram was the neighbor Asa was hoping would turn things around for him. That's a whole lot of treasure to put on a messenger's back, friends.

The word is "break." Asa says, "Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me." He wants Ben-hadad to walk away from his deal with Baasha. It's like asking someone to ditch their other plans and come help you instead.

The word is "abandons." When Baasha learned what had happened, "…he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work." The whole project just dropped. I think that's what a man does when he realizes the trouble has moved to his own cities.

The answer is True. The men of Judah "…carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building." Then Asa used those materials to build up Geba and Mizpah. Baasha's own supplies got turned into Asa's building projects, and that's recycling at a royal level.

The answer is that Asa relied on Aram and not the LORD. Hanani says, "Because you have relied on the king of Aram and not on the LORD your God…" The problem wasn't a lack of silver or a lack of armies. It was where Asa put his trust.

The answer is True. Hanani asks, "Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army with many chariots and horsemen?" Then he says, "Yet because you relied on the LORD, He delivered them into your hand." Hanani is pointing back to a time when Asa leaned on the LORD, and it went very differently.

The answer is to show Himself strong for devoted hearts. Hanani says, "For the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him." I love that line, friends. The LORD is looking over all the earth for people who are fully His.

The answer is "at war." Hanani tells Asa, "You have acted foolishly in this matter. From now on, therefore, you will be at war." Asa paid a pile of silver and gold to fix one problem. And Hanani says war is what's coming. That's one expensive deal.

The answer is that Asa puts him in prison. The text says Asa was angry and "…became so enraged over this matter that he put the man in prison." Hanani told him the truth, and Asa locked him up for it. I think that one hurts.
The answer is False. Asa put Hanani in prison, and "…at the same time Asa oppressed some of the people." So Hanani wasn't the only one Asa treated harshly. This is a heavy part of the story.

The word is "physicians." In his illness Asa "…did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians." The problem wasn't the doctors. It was that the LORD wasn't the one he sought. I think that's a sad line to read, friends.

The answer is in a tomb he cut out for himself. The text says Asa "…was buried in the tomb that he had cut out for himself in the City of David." He picked out his own resting place ahead of time. That's some serious planning.
